title: perf-bench-scratch-sam-park-2026-03-09
content:
Quick perf scratchpad - goal: sanity-check throughput/latency tradeoffs for 13B-class model variants on dedicated A100-80GB, test impact of batching + KV-cache + int8 quantization.

Environment:
- infra: dedicated-a100-80g (single GPU)
- runtime build: runtime/2026-03-08 (with continuous-batching fixes)
- models: redwood-13b-fp16 (baseline), redwood-13b-int8 (quantized), llama2-13b (comparison)
- client: local loadgen, steady-state 30s ramps, 3 warmup runs per config
- metrics captured: p50/p95 latency (ms), tokens/s throughput, GPU util, mem usage, kv-cache hit ratio

Test matrix (short):
- seq_len: 256, 1024, 2048
- batch_sizes: 1, 2, 4, 8
- kv-cache: cold vs warm (simulate dialogue reuse)
- quant: fp16 vs int8

Representative results (single-GPU):
- redwood-13b-fp16, seq=256:
  - batch=1: p50=85ms, p95=120ms, tokens/s=420
  - batch=4: p50=180ms, p95=260ms, tokens/s=1500
- redwood-13b-fp16, seq=1024:
  - batch=1: p50=320ms, p95=420ms, tokens/s=340
  - batch=4: p50=760ms, p95=980ms, tokens/s=1150
- redwood-13b-int8, seq=256, batch=1:
  - p50=72ms, p95=115ms, tokens/s=490 (roughly +17% throughput vs fp16 at batch=1)
- KV-cache (warm) impact, seq=1024, batch=1:
  - cold: p50=320ms, warm: p50=120ms (cache hit ratio ~93%) - big win for multi-turn dialogue

Observations / quick notes:
- Batching increases throughput linearly-ish up to GPU mem limits, but per-request latency grows and p95 tail becomes worse. For latency-sensitive routes (chat UI SLO=150ms p95) batching >2 is unsafe at seq>256.
- int8 gives consistent throughput improvement (~15-20%) at cost of slightly higher p95 variance in some runs. Need to validate output parity / QA on regen tests.
- KV cache dramatically reduces latency for typical dialogue patterns. Warm cache is the most important optimization for interactive chat.
- For long sequences (2048) GPU mem and kernel behavior cause large jumps in latency; consider recommended model windowing or prompt truncation for hosted-low-latency tier.
- GPU util at batch=4/8 saturates (~90%), but latency SLOs break for small interactive workloads - suggests routing policy should favor smaller batch sizes for low-tier customers or re-route to dedicated pools.

Action items / next steps:
- Re-run key configs with distributed traces enabled (trace ids) to collect per-kernel timings (INF-789).
- Add automated regen checks for int8 variant (compare token-level diffs on 1000-prompt set).
- Run same matrix on multi-GPU pod (2xA100) to measure parallelism scaling and KV-cache coherence costs.
- Instrument continuous-batching thresholds in runtime to avoid increasing p95 above 150ms for interactive routes - propose default max_batch_size=2 for routes tagged low-latency.
- Sync with Maya for dashboarding (per-route p95 vs batch size) and with Alex for cost modeling (tokens/s vs $/hour).

Notes to self:
- keep this doc messy; will move polished results to confluence after second pass.
- capture raw csvs from loadgen and attach to INF-789.

Unresolved questions:
- Is int8 stable across our full eval-suite? (need to check long-form coherency).
- How does quantization interact with kernel selection for 2k+ seqs? observed some kernel fallback thrashing.

End of scratchpad.
